text:
ash: Observed a regression in 0.12.4 python sdk where high fan-out async jobs stall. Repro with our onboarding sample that creates a new AsyncClient per request.
nina: Can you paste a tiny repro?
ash: Sure — super minimal below. No exceptions, tasks just queue and tail latency skyrockets.
```
# repro
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def one(i):
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        await c.generate('hi')

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(*[one(i) for i in range(350)])

asyncio.run(main())
```

leo: I bisected: PR that added a global semaphore defaulting to 100 (intended to protect httpcore) is the culprit. Downgrading to 0.12.3 removes the stall.
qa-bot: Temporary mitigation: reuse a single AsyncClient instance across tasks or pass AsyncClient(max_concurrency=500).
sam: For DX we should not surprise users. Many quickstarts instantiate per-request. Propose changing default to None and document best practices. Add env var RWD_PYSDK_MAX_CONCURRENCY for org-level caps.
nina: Also add CI test that runs a 400-concurrency gather to catch regressions. I'll open a PR and update sample apps.
ash: Filing INC-2026 for the customer demo hit by this.
sam: Good plan. Thanks — small docs + snippet should reduce onboarding friction.
leo: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/912 — change default to None, add env var, tests, docs.
qa-bot: deploy:staging started for 0.12.5-rc1 by nina
nina: Will run loadbench once rc is up and confirm. :thumbsup:
